summary: Session TTL slip causes hot-key cache miss storms and intermittent p99 latency on replayed turns
description: Issue summary: Multiple customers (first observed by Acme Retail) reported intermittent high p99 inference latency and occasional 504 timeouts when re-sending identical conversational turns (immediate replay of the previous user message). Impact: Replayed prompts that should hit warm prefix/session KV entries are falling back to cold-path lookups, causing expensive shard reads and downstream per-token tail latency spikes (~600-900ms additional per-token at p99) and occasional request timeouts. The issue is customer-facing for enterprise customers in us-east and correlates with a recent TTL sliding-window change deployed in kvcache two days prior. Environment: prod, us-east-1, mixed dedicated and hosted routing for the affected tenant. Observed against both redwood-open-3b and redwood-latency-optimized-7b variants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a conversational session with the customer account in prod us-east-1
2) Send a prompt that includes a ~1.2k token context followed by a short user utterance; record response latency
3) Immediately re-send the identical user utterance (simulate replay/duplicate user action)
4) Observe that the first replay frequently has warm-path latency but subsequent replays within a 2-5s window hit p99 spikes or timeout, rather than consistent warm hits
5) Reproduce several times and capture serving/runtime logs and kvcache trace ids
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: hot-key evictions or prefetch thrash. Observed different pattern: TTLs for session prefix keys are being decremented inconsistently across shards after the recent TTL sliding-window change (PR #2398).

Trace correlation shows the same session key sometimes present on initial request and missing on immediate replay within 1-3s—suggests per-shard TTL slip (race) where the key is treated expired on the replaying shard but present on requester shard, causing a cold-path backfill even for identical prompts.
Metric signals: kvcache cache-hit-rate for affected customer drops from 98% -> 72% for the replay window; p99 token latency for affected workloads increases by ~0.6-0.9s during miss storms.
Reproduction on staging with controlled shard mapping reproduces the miss when TTL update batching is enabled + high small-burst traffic. Disabling TTL batch commit removes the effect.
Immediate mitigations tested: enabling aggressive prefix pinning on routing reduces observed p99 by keeping requests on shards with warmed session keys (workaround only; not ideal for multi-AZ).
comments: Support (Sonia Alvarez) 2026-03-10: Customer reports intermittent 504s and high p99 on replay. Captured logs and sample request ids attached. Asking SRE to triage.
SRE (Marcus Patel) 2026-03-10: Assigned. Initial triage points to kvcache TTL behavior after last deployment (runtime PR #2398). Kicking off deeper trace correlation across shards.
Customer (Acme Retail - Eng) 2026-03-10: Impacting recommender UI; users see repeated 'slow' playback on re-try, trying to mitigate on their side increases complexity.
SRE 2026-03-11: Replayed tests on staging show TTL commit batching + high burst leads to inter-shard TTL race. Opened PR to make TTL commit atomic per-session-key (kvcache #441).

Support 2026-03-12: Notified customer of interim workaround: enable session_pin routing flag or increase session TTL to avoid sliding-window expiry during bursts. Planned production rollback of TTL sliding-window change if PR does not land quickly.
resolution: Workaround: For impacted enterprise customers (Acme Retail) we enabled session_pin routing (keeps requests to the warmed shard) and temporarily increased session TTL to 30s. This reduced p99 spikes by ~85% for the observed workload. Long-term fix: landed atomic TTL commit in kvcache (PR #441) and are rolling to prod in a controlled canary starting 2026-03-13. Post-rollback plan: if atomic commit is delayed, revert the TTL sliding-window change (runtime PR #2398) across us-east. Follow-ups: add end-to-end trace that tags TTL update origin so we can trace per-key TTL mutations, add an alert (kvcache.low_warm_hit_rate) to catch >10% drop for customer sessions, and run a blast-radius test prior to future TTL algorithm changes.
